publisher: Shell International (Royal Dutch Shell / Shell plc)
title: People and Connections: Global Scenarios to 2020 (public summary)
notes: Public summary dated Shell International 2002 (page footers 26 February 2002). Shell's 2005 report calls these "the 2001 Global Scenarios"; the edition id follows Shell's listing (2002).

entries.label: Business Class
entries.quote: The world of Business Class is not run by business; but it is run like a business with a focus on efficiency and individual freedom of choice.
entries.subject: global business environment

entries.label: Prism
entries.quote: Prism is a world that has gone beyond the modernist emphasis on efficiency, functionality, and global homogeneity toward the realisation of ‘multiple modernities’ that incorporate diverse cultural values and practices.
entries.subject: global business environment
global elite
entries.quote: In 2000, some 125 million people, from every country in the world, will qualify as members of the 'global elite'. By 2020 this could rise to over 300 million people.

entries.subject: natural gas
entries.quote: By 2020 ultimately recoverable world gas resources are much larger than estimated at the turn of the century, rising to 3300 billion barrels of oil equivalent.
entries.note: From the "Great Game of Gas" section under Business Class.

entries.subject: oil price
entries.quote: From the low in 2003, oil prices rise for the next few years, peaking in 2006 at $40/bbl.
entries.note: From "The Long Oil Game" section under Prism; money-of-the-day basis not stated.

entries.subject: renewable energy
entries.metric: renewables commercially viable in some markets
entries.quote: Strongly supported by governments, and led by wind power, renewables achieve commercial viability in some markets by 2010 and grow rapidly through to 2020.
